import Callout from '@/components/Callout.astro';

Open with the situation the reader is in. One or two short paragraphs — no "in this chapter we
will", no throat clearing.

## The first section

Start at `##`; the `<h1>` comes from `title`. Only `##` and `###` appear in the table of
contents.

```bash
# Always tag the language. Every command here must have been run before publishing.
some --command
```

<Callout type="note">
  Four types are available: `note`, `tip`, `warning` and `danger`. Use `danger` only for things
  that destroy data or create a security hole — if everything is a danger, nothing is.
</Callout>

### A subsection

Tables work and scroll horizontally on mobile with no extra markup:

| Thing | Meaning |
| ----- | ------- |
| A | B |

<Callout type="warning" title="Custom titles override the default label">
  Without a `title`, the callout prints its type name. With one, it prints yours.
</Callout>

## Where this goes wrong

The most valuable section of most chapters. What does everyone get wrong here, why does the tool
let them, and what does the error actually mean?

## Closing

One line pointing at the next chapter. The pager below already links it, so keep this short —
it is a handoff, not a summary.
